description: VeeInvite cultural content library. Defines every piece of content each culture needs, where it belongs on the wedding website, and what fields to collect from the couple. Drives the quiz step 2 configurator and the renderer section injection. Each culture has a default ceremony list (pre-selected) and an additional list (available but not pre-selected). Sub-regions override the default pre-selection but the full default list is always shown as optional.

sectionTypes.hero_eyebrow: Small label above couple names. Religious symbol, blessing, or opening invocation.
sectionTypes.hero_names_area: Area around couple names. Parents names, grandparents, family hosting line.
sectionTypes.hero_date_area: Below venue and date. Alternative calendar dates, auspicious time.
sectionTypes.hero_cta_area: Near RSVP button. Critical ceremony time, urgent notes for guests.
sectionTypes.story: Story section. Family narrative, how families are connected.
sectionTypes.events: Event cards. Each ceremony as its own card with time, venue, description.
sectionTypes.rsvp: RSVP form. Meal options, event selection, dietary.
sectionTypes.gallery: Photo gallery. Engagement, family, pre-wedding ceremony photos.
sectionTypes.faq: FAQ section. Dress code, cultural customs for guests, parking, accommodation.
sectionTypes.custom_section: New section inserted before footer. Content that does not fit existing sections.
sectionTypes.footer: Footer area. Secondary family names, closing blessing, cultural sign-off.

hindu_indian.copyTone: Formal and family-honoring. Parents invite on behalf of couple. Grand and celebratory.
hindu_indian.copyGuardrails: Never genericise sub-cultures. Tamil ≠ Punjabi ≠ Gujarati ≠ Bengali. Use correct ceremony names per sub-region. Never use 'Namaste' as a universal Indian greeting — it is North Indian. South Indian weddings do not use the same ceremony names as North Indian ones. Haldi is called Pithi in Gujarati, Gaye Holud in Bengali, Mangala Snanam in Tamil, Pellikuthuru in Telugu.

tamil.note: Distinct from North Indian. Ceremonies start at dawn at Muhurtham. Emphasis on Vedic purity. No Sangeet traditionally. Kashi Yatra is a beloved ritual.
tamil.copyNote: Tamil weddings are fundamentally different from North Indian weddings. Never use Sangeet, Pheras, Baraat, or Haldi as Tamil ceremony names. Correct Tamil terms: Nischayathartham (engagement), Mangala Snanam (purifying bath), Gauri Puja (bride worships Parvati), Kashi Yatra (groom pretends to leave), Oonjal (swing ceremony), Maalai Maatral (garland exchange), Kanyadaanam (giving away the bride), Saptapadi (seven steps), Ammi Midithal (foot on grinding stone). Haldi equivalent is Mangala Snanam or Pellikuthuru (Telugu) — not Haldi.

marathi.note: Ganesh Puja opens all ceremonies. Sakhar Puda is the engagement. Antarpat ritual — bride and groom do not see each other before ceremony. Mangal Sutra and Saptapadi (Satapadhi) central.
marathi.copyNote: Marathi weddings: Sakhar Puda is the engagement (not Sagai). Haldi is called Halad Chadavne. The Antarpat ritual separates bride and groom before ceremony. Kelvan is the family prayer ceremony. Mangalashtakas are Sanskrit verses recited at the key moment. Bride's maternal uncle escorts her to the mandap.

telugu.note: Similar to Tamil in many ways. Strong spiritual focus. Women are central participants. Talambralu (showering rice) is a unique and playful ritual. Pellikuthuru is the Haldi equivalent.
telugu.copyNote: Telugu weddings: Pellikuthuru (bride) and Pellikoduku (groom) are the Haldi equivalents — not Haldi. Nischayam is the engagement. Talambralu is unique — couple showers each other with rice and turmeric. Muhurtham is the auspicious ceremony time. Pallikonda Pelli is the post-wedding ritual where couple seeks blessings from elders.

kannada.note: Similar structure to other South Indian weddings. Naandi (ancestor blessing) is important. Post-wedding: Grihapravesh and Name Change ceremony are distinct Kannada traditions.
kannada.copyNote: Kannada weddings: Naandi is the ancestor blessing ceremony. The Name Change ceremony is unique — groom writes a new name for the bride on a plate of rice. Grihapravesh involves the bride overturning a rice vessel with her right foot. Seeru is the exchange of gifts between families.

kerala_malayali.note: Known for simplicity and elegance. Main ceremony lasts only 1-2 hours. Thalikettu (tying of Thali) is the central moment. Sadhya feast on banana leaf essential. Ceremonies performed at dawn during Muhurtham.
kerala_malayali.copyNote: Kerala Hindu weddings are elegant and brief — the main ceremony is 1-2 hours, not a full day. Thalikettu (Thali tying) is the central ritual. Nischayam is the engagement. Madhuparkam is when the bride's father welcomes the groom with a white saree. Sadhya is the traditional vegetarian feast on banana leaves — mention it. Do not import North Indian ceremony names.

marwari_rajasthani.note: Lavish and royal. Vibrant Rajasthani folk music and dance. Baraat on horse or elephant. Ganesh Puja opens all ceremonies. Mama (maternal uncle) has a special role.
marwari_rajasthani.copyNote: Marwari weddings are grand and royal. Haldi is called Pithi Dastoor (turmeric and sandalwood). Sangeet is called Mehfil. Engagement is called Sagai or Mudda Tikka. Roka is the informal agreement ceremony. Bhaat Nyotana is the maternal family invitation ceremony. Nikasi is the groom's procession preparation ritual. Telbaan is the ritual bath. First three Pheras led by bride, last four by groom — opposite of some other traditions.

jain.note: Simple and traditional. Marriage considered a worldly affair but encouraged. No fire ceremony for Digambar Jains. Bana Betai (chickpea flour) instead of Haldi. Pheras for Shwetambar Jains.
jain.copyNote: Jain weddings: Haldi equivalent is Bana Betai (chickpea flour paste, not turmeric) for Marwari Jains. Tel Baan is the Jain Haldi. Pheras — seven rounds — used in Shwetambar Jain weddings. Digambar Jains do not use fire in ceremony. No Baraat for Digambar Jains. Mehendi is called Mehendi (same). Engagement: Sagai or Khol Barana (Marwari Jain).

sikh.description: Faith-centered. The Anand Karaj is the Sikh marriage ceremony performed in the Gurdwara. Waheguru's blessing is central.
sikh.philosophy: Faith and family centered. Waheguru's blessing central. Marriage is a spiritual journey — Sikh ceremony conducted in Gurdwara in presence of Guru Granth Sahib.
sikh.designGuidance: Saffron (sacred Sikh color), navy blue, gold, white. Ik Onkar symbol (ੴ). Khanda symbol. Lotus and floral motifs. Marigolds feature prominently.

colorPalette.note: Sikh weddings center on saffron orange and navy blue — the sacred colors of the faith. Gold and marigold are always present.

bgPrimary.note: Deep Sikh navy — the Nishan Sahib flag background. Deep, dignified, spiritual.

accent.note: Sacred saffron orange — Kesri, the color of the Sikh flag and dastar (turban). Spiritually significant.

gold.note: Marigold gold — marigolds are central to Sikh wedding decoration and Gurdwara decor.

sikh.copyTone: Devotional and family-honoring. Waheguru's blessing invoked. Four Lavaan (rounds) central to Anand Karaj.
sikh.copyGuardrails: The Anand Karaj is conducted in the Gurdwara in the presence of the Guru Granth Sahib. It is a sacred ceremony — not a 'ceremony around fire'. Four Lavaan (circumbulations) are taken. Non-Sikh guests need guidance about Gurdwara customs (head covering, no shoes).

muslim.description: Faith-centered. The Nikah is the Islamic marriage contract — the spiritual heart of the wedding. Modesty and divine blessing are central.
muslim.philosophy: Faith-centered. Divine blessing framed as Allah's will. Family lineage honored. Nikah and Walima are the two essential events.
muslim.designGuidance: Green (Islamic significance), gold, white, deep blue. Arabic calligraphy as a design element. Geometric Islamic patterns. Persian roses, Mughal lotus, crescent moon motifs. No human figures in decorative elements.

colorPalette.note: Muslim wedding colors: green is sacred (Islam), gold is prosperity, deep blue is regal. Sub-regions vary — South Asian Muslim uses jewel tones, Arab uses white and gold, West African uses bold vibrant colors.

bgPrimary.note: Deep Islamic green — forest to emerald range. Green is the color of the Prophet and paradise in Islam.

accent.note: Islamic gold — prosperity and abundance. Always warm, never cold.

gold.note: Quran gold — the color of Arabic calligraphy and mosque ornamentation.

bgPrimary.note: Deep jewel purple or royal blue — South Asian Muslim weddings use rich jewel tones alongside Islamic green.

accent.note: Mehndi pink-rose — South Asian Muslim Mehndi ceremony colors. Warm and festive.

gold.note: South Asian wedding gold — warm marigold-influenced.

bgPrimary.note: Near-white or ivory — Arab Muslim weddings traditionally use white and gold. Purity and elegance.

accent.note: Rich Arab gold — the primary visual element on white. Zaffa procession gold.

gold.note: Arabian gold — warm, rich, and prominent.

bgPrimary.note: Deep Islamic green — West African Muslim weddings honor Islamic green prominently.

accent.note: Vibrant West African amber-gold — community celebration energy.

gold.note: Celebration gold — West African weddings are community events with vivid color.

muslim.copyTone: Devotional. Divine blessing framed as Allah's will. Formal and family-honoring. Bismillah is the opening.
muslim.copyGuardrails: No alcohol references anywhere on the site. No human figures in any AI-generated decorative elements. Do not mix Hindu religious references. Do not use Ganesh, Om, or Hindu ceremony names. Nikah is the Islamic marriage contract — not a 'ceremony'. Walima is an obligation for the groom's family, not just a party.

south_asian_muslim.copyNote: South Asian Muslim weddings include Mehndi. They follow Islamic tradition (Nikah, Walima) but may also include South Asian pre-wedding customs. Do not confuse with Hindu ceremonies — no Pheras or Saptapadi.

arab_muslim.note: Arab Muslim weddings may have separate celebrations for men and women. Mahr (dowry) is part of the Nikah contract.
arab_muslim.copyNote: Arab Muslim weddings may involve gender-segregated celebrations. Zaffa (wedding procession with music) is common in Levantine and Egyptian traditions. Mahr is the mandatory gift from groom to bride.

west_african_muslim.note: West African Muslim weddings blend Islamic tradition with West African community customs. Community celebration is large.
west_african_muslim.copyNote: West African Muslim weddings are community-centered. Nikah and Walima follow Islamic tradition. Community celebration may be large and vibrant.

chinese.description: Family-centered. The banquet is as important as the ceremony. Parents send invitations on behalf of the couple. Cash in red envelopes is the gift tradition.
chinese.philosophy: Family-centered. The banquet is the focal social event. Both parents' names are a key mark of respect.
chinese.designGuidance: Red (#CC0000 range) and gold (#D4A853 range) are traditional and expected. Double happiness character (囍) nearly always present. Dragon and phoenix imagery. Mandarin ducks. Peonies, cherry blossoms, plum blossoms. High contrast, celebratory — not subtle or minimal.

colorPalette.note: Chinese weddings: red is non-negotiable (luck, happiness, prosperity). Gold is always paired with red. Never white as primary (mourning). Never black as primary.

bgPrimary.note: Chinese ceremonial red — the precise range of Chinese wedding red. #CC0000 is the reference point. Vivid, not dark maroon. Not burgundy.

accent.note: Imperial gold — always warm yellow-gold for Chinese weddings, never rose gold. The color of the emperor.

gold.note: Chinese festive gold — bright, celebratory. The 囍 character is always rendered in gold.

chinese.copyTone: Family-honoring. Both parents' names prominently listed. Banquet as the focal event. Auspicious language throughout.
chinese.copyGuardrails: Red and gold are not optional — they are culturally expected. The 囍 symbol should appear. No white (mourning color in Chinese tradition) as primary color. Do not use Western casualness in copy — this is a family-honoring formal invitation.

jewish.description: Joy-centered and family-honoring. Simcha (joy) is the guiding tone. The Chuppah time is critical — guests must not miss it.
jewish.philosophy: Simcha (joy) guides the tone. Both families co-host. Chuppah time must be prominent and impossible to miss.
jewish.designGuidance: Deep blue and gold most traditional. Star of David, Tree of Life, Jerusalem imagery. Ornate Hebrew calligraphy if used. Some couples include a Ketubah-inspired border.

colorPalette.note: Jewish weddings: deep blue (royal color of King David) and gold are most traditional. White and ivory also appropriate. Many modern Jewish couples choose any palette — the cultural signal comes from symbols not colors.

bgPrimary.note: Royal Davidic blue — deep, regal. Blue appears on Ketubah designs and Jewish wedding invitations. Not navy-black, genuinely blue.

accent.note: Ketubah gold — the gold of illuminated manuscripts and Ketubah artwork. Warm and scholarly.

gold.note: Jerusalem gold — the color of Jerusalem stone at sunset. Warm and ancient.

jewish.copyTone: Joyful and warm. 'Share in our Simcha' not 'Request the honor of your presence'. Both families co-host equally. Hebrew phrases used with respect.
jewish.copyGuardrails: Never use Christian or Islamic references. Tone is Simcha (joy) not formality. The Chuppah time must be impossible to miss — guests must be seated before it begins. Shabbat restrictions apply for Friday/Saturday weddings. Hebrew text is sacred — do not use casually.

nigerian_yoruba.description: Community-centered. Multiple events across different days. Aso-ebi (matching fabric) connects the community visually.
nigerian_yoruba.philosophy: Community-centered. Extended family prominent. Multiple ceremonies across days. Aso-ebi is essential — guests wear matching fabric.
nigerian_yoruba.designGuidance: Vibrant rich colors — purple, gold, royal blue, emerald green. African print-inspired borders and patterns. Photos of the couple are common. Bold and celebratory.

colorPalette.note: Yoruba weddings: Aso-ebi determines the color. Purple and gold is the most iconic combination. Emerald green and gold, royal blue and gold, and deep navy with orange are all authentic. Colors are rich, jewel-toned, and never muted.

bgPrimary.note: Royal Yoruba purple — the most iconic Yoruba wedding color. Deep, rich, and regal.

accent.note: Celebration gold — purple and gold is the definitive Yoruba wedding combination.

nigerian_yoruba.copyGuardrails: Do not generalise to 'African'. Yoruba-specific references are appropriate. Igba Nkwu is Igbo — not Yoruba. Yoruba traditional ceremony is the Introduction. Never use South Asian or Hindu cultural references.

nigerian_igbo.description: Community-centered. The Igba Nkwu wine-carrying ceremony is the symbolic heart of the Igbo traditional wedding.
nigerian_igbo.philosophy: Community and family centered. The Igba Nkwu (wine carrying) is the most symbolic traditional ceremony — bride carries palm wine to find her groom among the guests.
nigerian_igbo.designGuidance: Rich and vibrant — deep reds, gold, royal blue. George fabric patterns. Bold and celebratory.

colorPalette.note: Igbo weddings: George wrapper fabric inspires the palette. Deep reds, royal blue, and rich gold are authentic. Igbo Blouse (handcrafted with local materials) uses intricate patterns. Coral beads (Bini brides) are distinctive.

nigerian_igbo.copyTone: Community-honoring. The Igba Nkwu is the spiritual union — mention it with respect. George fabric and aso-ebi are central to the visual identity.
nigerian_igbo.copyGuardrails: Igbo ≠ Yoruba. Igba Nkwu is specific to Igbo tradition. Do not use Yoruba terms for Igbo events. Never generalise to 'African'.

latin_american_catholic.description: Family and community honor. The padrino (godparent/sponsor) system is central. Catholic Mass is the ceremony.
latin_american_catholic.philosophy: Family and community honor. Padrinos are recognized publicly on the invitation. Catholic Mass is the ceremony anchor.
latin_american_catholic.designGuidance: Elaborate and ornate. Floral motifs — roses, dahlias. Gold and deep reds, jewel tones. Bilingual Spanish and English for diaspora families.

colorPalette.note: Latin American Catholic weddings vary by country. Mexican-inspired: vibrant reds, pinks, and golds. Colombian/Venezuelan: jewel tones with gold. Formal Catholic: deep burgundy and cream. All feature warm, celebratory colors.

accent.note: Rosa Mexicana pink — the iconic hot pink of Mexican celebrations. Or warm rose for more formal weddings.
